hypothesis_text: Patients taking antihypertensives have lower blood pressure levels compared to those not taking them.
Individuals prescribed antidepressants report improved mood compared to those not prescribed antidepressants.
Taking antihypertensives is associated with reduced risk of dementia onset.
Taking antidepressants is associated with slower decline in cognitive function over time.
Long-term use of antihypertensives is linked to better overall cognitive performance in older adults.
Depression symptoms are more common among individuals who do not take antidepressants.
Cognitive flexibility is negatively associated with MMSE score.
Lower MMSE scores are linked to reduced cognitive flexibility.
Individuals with higher MMSE scores show greater cognitive flexibility.
Higher levels of anxiety are associated with greater use of antipsychotics.
Patients with moderate to severe anxiety are more likely to receive antipsychotic medication than those with low anxiety.
Antipsychotic use is positively associated with self-reported anxiety symptoms.
Men with mild cognitive impairment have worse cognitive scores than women with mild cognitive impairment.
Women with mild cognitive impairment have better cognitive scores than men with mild cognitive impairment.
Sex is not associated with the presence or severity of mild cognitive impairment.
Smoking is negatively associated with processing speed.
Individuals who smoke have slower processing speeds than non-smokers.
Current smokers show worse processing speed compared to never-smokers.
Patients who undergo heart valve replacement have a higher prevalence of metabolic syndrome compared to those who do not.
Metabolic syndrome is associated with an increased risk of requiring heart valve replacement.
Individuals with metabolic syndrome are more likely to need heart valve replacement surgery than individuals without metabolic syndrome.
Individuals with the APOE ε4 allele have a lower likelihood of being prescribed antihypertensives.
Patients taking antihypertensives show reduced risk of APOE-related cognitive decline.
The presence of APOE ε4 is associated with higher blood pressure levels.
Antihypertensive use is independently associated with lower APOE ε4 carrier frequency in older adults.
Regular aspirin use is associated with improved attention in older adults.
Individuals who take aspirin daily show better attention scores compared to non-users.
There is no association between aspirin use and attention performance.
Individuals with metabolic syndrome are less likely to take aspirin regularly.
People with metabolic syndrome have a lower incidence of cardiovascular events if they take aspirin daily.
